changelog: - **A Gate that takes resources from more than one place now plans with the Converter it feeds, so nothing it passes on is lost.** A Gate fed by two upstream Gates or Converters, or by one of them and its own Pool, kept the earlier behaviour: each supply delivered its full amount before the Converter after the Gate had decided how much of its recipe it could run, and the difference was lost (the run strip said how much). Now such a Gate is planned together with its group, and its supplies are filled one after the other in a fixed order — the upstream Gates and Converters in the running order, then the Gate's own Pool connections in their order — each to the most the group can take with the earlier ones in place. The first supply therefore has priority, the later ones get what the Converter still has room for, and nothing is lost. A `pull all` Gate with two supplies asks for the most each supply could carry on its own and moves at that amount or not at all; when a Pool it reads is also read by its Converter and both cannot be met, the whole group moves nothing. Two Gates merging into one with no Converter behind them, as in the gacha Templates, are planned the same way, so when their target is nearly full the first Gate fills it and the second holds back, instead of both delivering and the surplus vanishing. Two such Gates whose paths meet at one Converter are planned together: the first in the running order is filled first, and the second brings exactly what the Converter can still take from it. A saved Monte Carlo distribution computed before this change opens marked as from an earlier version of the engine until you run it again. None of the bundled examples changes.
